text:
maria: Quick audit of the overnight continuous-batching runs. kbench across A10/T4/L4/A100/H100. Found a couple of things: p95 regression on A100 when KV fragmentation > 30%, and H100 throughput drop on mixed short+long workloads. Putting raw notes here for triage.

sam: can you paste the perf numbers (p50/p95/throughput) so we can see scale?

maria: sure, pasted core table from the job: ```
GPU    | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | throughput(tok/s) | notes
A10    | 42      | 190     | 6200              | good packing, kernel_v1 wins small seqs
T4     | 58      | 240     | 4200              | fine
L4     | 36      | 170     | 6800              | best cost/latency for small requests
A100   | 34      | 270     | 7600              | p95 reg when KV-frag > 30% (see below)
H100   | 30      | 235     | 6900              | throughput drops ~12% on mixed short/long
```

chen: what were the max_tokens_per_batch settings for this run?

maria: config snapshot: ```
max_tokens_per_batch: { A10: 8192, T4: 6144, L4: 8192, A100: 16384, H100: 16384 }
max_batch_size: { A10: 128, T4: 96, L4: 128, A100: 256, H100: 256 }
batch_queue_policy: "latency_slo_preemptive"
kernel_selector: "auto:v1->v2"
kv_cache_prefetch: true
```

ada: the A100 p95 jump looks KV-frag related — do we have the KV-frag distribution?

maria: yes — fragmentation bucketed by slice: ```
KV-frag % | pct_requests
0-10      | 64%
10-30     | 20%
30-60     | 10%  <-- where p95 blows up
60+       | 6%   <-- pathological, long seqs + slicing
```

sam: hypothesis: large max_tokens_per_batch on A100 encourages aggressive packing which increases KV cache churn and fragmentation, causing kernel_v2 to pick a slower path for lookups?

maria: exactly. The kernel selector falls back to the safe KV lookup path when fragment > 30% and sequence > 512. That safe path is ~30-40% slower at p95 for A100.

chen: what about H100 regression — mixed workloads mean small requests get packed with long ones and warmup + kernel selection thrash?

maria: profiling trace shows many short requests waiting for a slice to complete, then long requests produce large KV writes that invalidate prefixes; effective throughput drops because we lose batching locality. H100's kernel_v1->v2 heuristics don't favor the warmed path in this mix.

ada: actionable suggestions?

maria: propose a few safe tuning steps to test:
1) Reduce max_tokens_per_batch for A100/H100 to 12288 to lower KV-frag onset.
2) Keep A10/L4 higher (8192 or bump A10 to 9216) — packing improves utilization there and KV-frag is rare.
3) Add an entropy-aware packing gate: avoid packing requests with seq_len>1024 with many short seqs (threshold on variance in batch formation).
4) Adjust kernel_selector rule: prefer kernel_v2 only when seq_mean>512 AND kv_frag<25%.
5) Change queue policy for mixed traffic to "size_stability_first" for 10% of slices (canary).

sam: can we simulate impact quickly? Run kbench with the tightened A100/H100 token cap and the new kernel_selector rule. We need p95 and throughputs plus KV-frag distribution.

maria: I already ran a 2-hour canary on a small shard: results looked promising. A100 p95 dropped from 270ms -> 220ms (~18% improvement) and throughput stable. H100 throughput regained ~9%. KV-frag 30-60 bucket shrank from 10%->4%.

chen: nice. Did that affect cost or missed packing opportunities on A10/L4?

maria: A10/L4 unchanged in that canary. But global rollout with gating will leave A10/L4 pack settings as-is. We only change A100/H100 caps.

ada: what's the rollback plan if we see regressions?

maria: rollout plan: canary 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% with realtime SLO checks (p95 < baseline+5%, throughput delta < 3%). If fail, auto-revert to previous token caps and kernel_selector via rollout-controller.

sam: add experiments to the dashboard and mark the tunable names so we can snapshot quickly. Also create a follow-up to test high-entropy workloads (web search style) vs low-entropy (chat).

infra-bot: perf job created: https://perf.redwood/investigations/1781234567 - kbench runs + traces attached.

maria: next actions: @sam run full 12h kbench on A100/H100 with new caps and kernel rule; @chen add entropy-aware gate flag (runtime tunable: batch_entropy_gate_p95_threshold=0.2); @ada add fallback unit test for kernel_selector so we don't accidentally flip to unsafe path.

sam: acked, starting runs this morning. Will post results to the perf link. :thumbsup:

chen: putting flag on staging now, will demo later today.

ada: I'll draft a short blurb for ops with the rollout steps and revert commands.

maria: thanks everyone — goal is to stabilize p95 on A100/H100 without hurting A10/L4. Will follow up with concrete numbers after sam's 12h run.

infra-bot: alert: scheduled canary monitor configured for p95, throughput, and kv_frag buckets. Rollout-controller will auto-stop on breach.
